assessment.title: What's Your PATH Score?
assessment.subtitle: Fourteen quick questions show how ready your savings are to pay you, and which of the four parts of your plan needs attention first: your Paycheck, your Assets, your Taxes, and your Heirs.
bullets: A score for each step: Paycheck, Assets, Taxes, Heirs
Your top focus areas, and what to do about them

questions.text: Do you know how much income the two of you will need each year in retirement?
Do you know where each dollar of that income will come from: Social Security, pensions, savings, rentals?

options.label: Yes, by source and by year

questions.text: Have you decided when each of you will claim Social Security, based on the numbers?
If the market dropped 25% the year you retire, do you know what it would do to your income?
Is the money you'll live on in the next few years invested differently from your long-term money?

options.label: No, it's all invested the same way

questions.text: Do you have a plan for a long-term care need for either of you?
questions.help: Home care, assisted living, or nursing care.

questions.text: Do you know how much of your savings is pre-tax (traditional IRA or 401(k)) versus Roth or taxable?
Has anyone shown you, year by year, what your required withdrawals and tax brackets could look like in retirement?

options.label: Yes, a CPA or planner has

questions.text: Has anyone reviewed whether Roth conversions make sense for you?
Do your financial advisor and your tax preparer talk to each other about your plan?
Do you have a will or trust that has been reviewed in the last 5 years?
Have you each named someone to make financial and medical decisions if you can't (powers of attorney)?

options.label: Yes, both kinds, for both of us

questions.text: Are the beneficiaries on your retirement accounts and life insurance up to date?
If one of you died tomorrow, would the other know where everything is and what to do first?

qualifiers.text: Roughly how much do you have saved for retirement, not counting your home?
qualifiers.help: A range is fine. It helps us point you to the right next step.

bands.label: No Path Yet
bands.headline: You've saved. You just don't have a path to run on yet.
bands.message: That's where most people start. Your money was built to grow, not to pay you. A few decisions made now can change how confident you feel about the years ahead.

bands.label: Path Under Construction
bands.headline: You've done real work. There are gaps that could cost you.
bands.message: You have a foundation. Your focus areas below show where a plan could make the biggest difference.

bands.label: On the Path
bands.headline: You're ahead of most people. A few refinements could matter a lot.
bands.message: Your plan is in good shape. Tightening your focus areas helps your income, your tax bill, and your family.

bands.label: Path to Run On
bands.headline: Excellent. You've covered the big pieces.
bands.message: Walking your PATH once a year keeps a strong plan strong as tax laws, markets, and your family change.

paycheck.low: You don't have a clear picture of your retirement paycheck yet: what you need, where it comes from, and the gap. Everything else builds on this.
paycheck.mid: You have a rough picture. A written Retirement Paycheck Map shows where every dollar comes from, by year, for both of you.
paycheck.high: Strong. You know your numbers and your income sources.

assets.low: A bad market early in retirement, or a long-term care need, could knock your income off course. Both can be planned for.
assets.mid: Some protection is in place. Check how your near-term income money is positioned, and your long-term care plan.
assets.high: Strong. Your money has jobs, and you've planned for the big risks.

taxes.low: Part of your 401(k) or IRA belongs to the IRS, and the rules decide when they collect. A tax plan decides it on your terms.
taxes.mid: You've thought about taxes. A year-by-year tax timeline, built from your actual return, often shows opportunities you're missing.
taxes.high: Strong. You're managing retirement taxes on purpose.

heirs.low: Without current documents and beneficiaries, your spouse and kids could face delays, court, and hard decisions at the worst time. This is often the fastest area to fix.
heirs.mid: You've started. Updating documents and beneficiaries keeps your wishes in force.
heirs.high: Strong. Your family is protected on paper.

capture.headline: Your score is ready. Where should we send it?
capture.text: Enter your name and email to see your score and your focus areas. We'll email you a copy too.
capture.smsConsent: Yes, Balanced Financial may text me about my results and upcoming classes. Message and data rates may apply. Reply STOP to opt out. Consent is not a condition of any purchase.
capture.privacyNote: We respect your privacy. We never sell your information.

appointment.name: PATH Review
appointment.headline: Turn your score into a path to run on.
appointment.text: In a complimentary 60-minute PATH Review, in our Fort Collins office or by Zoom, Greg walks through your Paycheck, Assets, Taxes, and Heirs with you, starting with your focus areas.
appointment.deliverable: Your one-page PATH Map: where you stand on all four steps and your top three gaps. It's yours to keep.
appointment.scarcity: Greg holds a limited number of PATH Reviews each month. No cost, no obligation.

nurture.headline: Your next step: The Tax Trap class.
nurture.text: Join Greg's free online class on the taxes hiding in your 401(k) and IRA, and how the PATH Plan handles them. Bring your questions.
